correctness.rationale: PASS. The n open-neighborhood facets are F_i={i-2,i-1,i+1,i+2}, n>=9. The omitted edge e_i={i-1,i+1} occurs in no other facet, so local barycentric map (u,c,d,v)->(u+m,c-m,d-m,v+m), m=min(c,d), linearly homotoped from identity, fixes overlaps between tetrahedra and retracts onto the two triangles A_i=[i-2,i+1,i+2], B_i=[i-2,i+2,i-1]. Every dihedral symmetry preserves which opposite edge is removed, so local retractions glue equivariantly. The core has (f0,f1,f2)=(n,3n,2n); each vertex link is a six-cycle, and the oriented sum of A_i+B_i has zero integral boundary, so it is a connected oriented closed surface of Euler characteristic zero, hence a torus. No nontrivial rotation stabilizes a vertex, edge or triangle and thus no point of the surface. Each reflection has no fixed triangle: odd n, one fixed vertex plus three swapped-edge midpoints; even n, two plus two or zero plus four. All cases have four isolated points, with fixed sets disjoint across different reflections since products are free rotations. Every element preserves surface orientation, so Riemann–Hurwitz on the 2n-sheet quotient gives sphere with four order-two branch orbits; C_n quotient remains a torus. Simplicial signed Lefschetz trace gives H1 trace 2 for rotations and -2 for reflections; with finite order, their integral matrices are +I and -I respectively. Independently rebuilt all core links, oriented boundaries, rotation fixed simplices and every reflection count for n=9..29. The all-n deformation and surface topology are proved directly, not by these finite tests; the original 3-dimensional complex itself is not claimed homeomorphic to a surface.
residual_risks: Orbifold signature is for torus core K_n; X_n/D_n is only homotopy equivalent to S2, not claimed a literal surface quotient.
Every reflection acts by -I on Z^2, not by an orientation-reversing torus map: det(-I)=+1; the checked oriented top cycle confirms consistency.
